title: Meeting Chris Kelly and playing for the Jamaicans' house parties
summary: Jiles filled in for Chris Kelly's drummer, then formed a band with Lawrence Toker, Melvin Frank and Bill Hamilton to play for Jamaican sailors.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: No bass, piano? No piano player. I see. Well that's the first band I started playing with. After my uncle took me to Old Man's Shalow there. That was the first band. And on the way from that house I met Chris Kelly, he was playing Lawn Party and Faye Soda drummer, that was a guy I admired too, was a great drummer. And he asked me to help him carry his drum while he was playing. And so I was telling him, I was going to less and taking up drums. I'll let you work out tonight. So I got on the drum and started playing. So Chris Kelly asked me who I was playing with. I told him I wasn't playing with nobody. He started out. He let me see him. He said, Cus, do you think you can play with me tomorrow night? I said yeah. So I went on and played with him. Played on Ivorville and Murray. Homes that are big rumming place. There's a lot of Jew makers in town. He started playing over there. And these guys didn't have no passport when they came over in America. And the immigration officer was rounding them up. He broke in and stopped the band. He said, what's your name? He said, tell his name, tell you stand on the side. He thought I looked so much like a Jew maker, asked me with my name. And when I told him he said it was all right. Because he could tell by the accent that I wasn't a Jew maker. And that's when they made up that song, Going Back Home to Jamaica. When they were singing all the Jamaicans back. They didn't have their passports. They were hired away over in this country. So after that, this lady, many times Chris Kelly would blow up. So she asked me, did I think I could get a band to play for? So I got Lawrence Toker, trumpet player. And we made up a band. A fellow they called Melvin Frank. He's a clarinet player. He did. And Bill Hamilton. He's living. He don't play anymore. He's a bass player and a banjo player. But we four took over the job. And from then on, we were playing the job for these Jew makers. It wasn't, it was a house party. You would say it wasn't a dance hall. Practically they'd come in on the ship and it was mostly Jew makers would be at the dance.
